workspace.question: How can DIKWP white-box claims be independently replicated on open-weight models?
workspace.reason: Peer-reviewed semantic-security anchors exist, but external replication of the broader artificial-consciousness stack remains the highest-value gap.

workspace.question: What falsifiable experiment separates purpose-aware control from prompt-conditioned language behavior?
workspace.reason: This is the bridge from DIKWP theory to a field-recognizable empirical result.

workspace.question: How should the 173-repository portfolio be consolidated into a canonical, contributor-friendly flagship architecture?
workspace.reason: Repository volume is high while release, project-board and external-maintainer signals are comparatively weak.

contradictions.resolution: Do not average. Declare date, scope, unit and counting rule; request a canonical ledger.

hypotheses.statement: A DIKWP purpose-conditioned audit layer will detect and prevent a measurable class of goal-drift and semantic-security failures better than output-only evaluation.
hypotheses.evidence_gap: No multi-lab preregistered comparison on a shared open-weight benchmark.
hypotheses.falsifier: No statistically meaningful improvement over strong output-only and generic trace baselines.

hypotheses.statement: Purpose representations that remain stable across task paraphrase, tool changes and adversarial reward perturbations have a causal role distinguishable from surface instruction following.
hypotheses.evidence_gap: No preregistered causal intervention across multiple model families and purpose encodings.
hypotheses.falsifier: Interventions fail to transfer or are fully explained by prompt/token artifacts.

hypotheses.statement: Consolidating repeated prototypes into five canonical organs with releases, tests and maintainers will increase external reuse and issue-based collaboration without reducing idea generation.
hypotheses.evidence_gap: No controlled portfolio intervention with before/after repository-health measures.
hypotheses.falsifier: After two release cycles, contributor, replication and maintenance indicators do not improve.

experiments.question: A DIKWP purpose-conditioned audit layer will detect and prevent a measurable class of goal-drift and semantic-security failures better than output-only evaluation.
experiments.design: 2x2 preregistered evaluation: DIKWP audit layer present/absent × benign/adversarial purpose shift, across two open-weight model families and two agent environments.
experiments.success: Primary measure improves beyond preregistered threshold and the result is independently reproducible.
experiments.failure: No statistically meaningful improvement over strong output-only and generic trace baselines.

experiments.question: Purpose representations that remain stable across task paraphrase, tool changes and adversarial reward perturbations have a causal role distinguishable from surface instruction following.
experiments.design: Causal representation study using paraphrase, tool swap, reward perturbation and activation intervention. Compare token-level, probe-level and behavior-level explanations.
experiments.success: Primary measure improves beyond preregistered threshold and the result is independently reproducible.
experiments.failure: Interventions fail to transfer or are fully explained by prompt/token artifacts.

experiments.question: Consolidating repeated prototypes into five canonical organs with releases, tests and maintainers will increase external reuse and issue-based collaboration without reducing idea generation.
experiments.design: Twelve-week portfolio intervention: baseline 30 days, migration into five organs, two tagged releases, then compare external issues, forks, repeat users, test coverage and maintainer latency.
experiments.success: Primary measure improves beyond preregistered threshold and the result is independently reproducible.
experiments.failure: After two release cycles, contributor, replication and maintenance indicators do not improve.
